summary: User reported that signalWithStart doesn't propagate requestId from WorkflowOptions, using a random UUID instead. Investigation revealed this is intentional—setRequestId is internal-only API that will be removed to prevent confusion.
userImpact: Users mistakenly believe they can provide an idempotency key for signalWithStart via WorkflowOptions, but this feature is internal-only and unreliable.
rootCause: The setRequestId method is documented as internal-only (not clearly communicated), and newSignalWithStartWorkflowExecutionRequest intentionally generates a fresh UUID.
proposedFix: Remove setRequestId from the public WorkflowOptions API to eliminate the confusion about whether it's user-facing.
resolutionDetails: The behavior is intentional—setRequestId is internal SDK functionality, not a public contract. The team will remove it from WorkflowOptions.
keyQuote: setRequestId is NOT intended to be called by user code it is meant for internal functionality
